content.text:
Booking works again: `createAppointment` in `src/repos/appointments.ts` inserted into a `created_by` column, but the schema calls it `created_by_user_id`. I corrected the column name, and a new test now books as Ava with Rosa and gets a 201 with an `apt_…` id. Typecheck and all 19 tests pass.

`route()` in `src/lib/http.ts` now handles unexpected errors by writing one error log line with an `errorId`, the route (method and path) and a cause. It then returns `{ "errorId": "err_<uuid>" }` with the 500. The cause holds only the error name, code, errno and SQL state, plus the message. The `sql` text and values are left out, and quoted values in the message are redacted, except for unknown-column and missing-table errors, which stay readable. The booking request carries no patient data in its URL, so Apache's access log has nothing to leak. I didn't add a test for the 500 path itself, so the `errorId` logging and redaction are untested.

`route()` in `src/lib/http.ts` now handles unexpected errors by writing one error log line with an `errorId`, the route (method and path) and a cause. It then returns `{ "errorId": "err_<uuid>" }` with the 500. The cause holds only the error name, code, errno and SQL state, plus the message. The `sql` text and values are left out, and quoted values in the message are redacted, except for unknown-column and missing-table errors, which stay readable. The booking request carries no patient data in its URL, so Apache's access log has nothing to leak. I didn't add a test for the 500 path itself, so the `errorId` logging and redaction are untested.
